checks.name: Class vocabulary
checks.output: The vocabulary is closed in code and checked at build time, so an invalid entry is refused at parse rather than discouraged. inventory.py declares KINDS (7), CLASSES (3: compatibility-only, durable, presentation-only), DISPOSITIONS (the 3 classes plus unclassified, out-of-scope, withheld) and SPELLING_FORMS (literal, legacy-suffix, name-family), and Declaration.validate refuses anything else. Negative controls, each observed: disposition 'mostly-durable' raised "declaration for 'x' has disposition 'mostly-durable', which is not one of ['compatibility-only', 'durable', 'presentation-only', 'unclassified', 'out-of-scope', 'withheld']"; kind 'table' raised "has kind 'table', which is not one of [...]"; spelling form 'freehand' raised "has spelling form 'freehand', which is not one of ['literal', 'legacy-suffix', 'name-family']". Positive control beside each: inventory.durable('command').validate('automonique status') is accepted, and test_the_generated_document_uses_only_the_closed_vocabularies re-reads the checked-in file and asserts every entry's kind, class and spelling_form is a member. A name fitting no class is an explicit finding, not a fourth class: `unclassified` is a declaration disposition that routes the name into the `unclassified` array with a required reason, and build() refuses an unclassified declaration whose reason is empty. All three classes are exercised on real data (140 / 17 / 2) and build() raises 'the closed class vocabulary is not exercised' if any class count reaches zero, which is what stops presentation-only from becoming a vocabulary entry nothing uses. The two presentation-only entries are `Monique` (package - docs/product-plan/requirements/client-experience-and-surfaces.md: 'presentation-only signed assets/animations with no tools, secrets or authority. Monique is the first-party mascot') and `AssistantPreviewDelta` (protocol - docs/product-plan/requirements/agent-integrations.md: '`AssistantPreviewDelta` - ephemeral presentation only'); both are labelled presentation-only by the source itself rather than by this item's judgement.

checks.name: Forwarding integrity
checks.output: All 17 compatibility-only entries name an existing durable counterpart in this same inventory, a reason, and the permitted source that binds the two; build() closes the forward against the durable set and raises before anything is written if it dangles. The 17 forwards, measured from the checked-in file: .legacy-current->.automonique-current, .legacy-releases->.automonique-releases, @legacy->@automonique, @legacy/*->@automonique, @legacy/sdk*->@automonique/sdk*, @legacy/sdk/connector->@automonique/sdk/connector, @legacy/sdk/provider->@automonique/sdk/provider, LEGACY_*->AUTOMONIQUE_*, LEGACY_RUNNER->AUTOMONIQUE_RUNNER, legacy-say->automonique-say, legacy-shell->automonique-shell, legacy-shot->automonique-shot, legacy-tui->automonique tui, legacy:audit->automonique audit, legacyctl->automonique (also automonique audit, doctor, reload, rollback, status, tui), legacyctl tui->automonique tui, legacyd->automonique daemon. Negative controls, each observed: a compatibility-only declaration with no forwards_to raised "declaration for 'legacy-nowhere' is compatibility-only and names no durable identifier to forward to; it would forward to nothing"; one with no reason raised 'is compatibility-only and must say why the compatibility surface exists'; and repointing `legacyd` at 'automonique nonexistent-subcommand' failed the whole build with "compatibility-only entry 'legacyd' forwards to 'automonique nonexistent-subcommand', which is not a durable entry in this inventory; it would forward to nothing". Positive control: test_every_forward_in_the_checked_in_copy_resolves re-reads the generated file and asserts every forwards_to and every forwards_to_also member is in durable_names. `legacyctl` is the one alias whose primary target is the binary rather than a subcommand, because docs/product-plan/requirements/target-architecture.md installs it as a thin shim that execs `automonique <subcommand>`; the six subcommand bindings other permitted sources state are carried in forwards_to_also rather than collapsed into one, so a consumer can test membership instead of equality. The generator opens exactly two kinds of path: files under docs/product-plan/ (via read()/corpus_files()) and its own output under plan/inventory/. checks.name: Scrub hygiene
checks.command: python3 tools/identifiers/test_inventory.py (ScrubHygiene.*); python3 plan/check.py --verify with the predecessor prefix planted in plan/inventory/identifiers.json, then with it removed
checks.output: No private identifier, personal address, host name or absolute home path appears in the inventory, and the generator refuses to write one rather than merely not writing one. render() runs the whole serialized document through scrub() before returning bytes, and scrub() refuses (a) the predecessor's identifier prefix, matched by SHA-256 fingerprint over lowercased word tokens of the declared length so this file never spells it, (b) /home/, /Users/, /root/ and ~/, (c) an email address, (d) a bare IPv4 address, (e) a third-party host name. Negative controls, each observed and each paired with a positive control. Legacy identifier: the test reads the value out of docs/product-plan/reference/legacy-inventory.md by fingerprint - never writing it - and feeds it to scrub(), which raised 'a test string names a legacy identifier (the predecessor system's identifier prefix); plan/inventory/identifiers.json is not one of the locations plan/gates.md#gate-scrub permits it in', and the assertion checks the message itself does not contain the value; the neutral string 'canonical AUTOMONIQUE_RUNNER, alias LEGACY_RUNNER, package @automonique/sdk, schema automonique.dev-metrics/v1' passes. '/home/operator/notes.md' raised 'carries a absolute home path'; 'person@example.com' raised 'personal email address'; '10.20.30.40' raised 'bare IP address'; 'console.internal' raised 'host name'. Anti-vacuity: replacing the fingerprint digest with 64 zeroes made guard_scrub_rules raise 'the legacy-identifier fingerprints match nothing in docs/product-plan/reference/legacy-inventory.md, so the scrub rule proves nothing'; the live fingerprint passes the same guard, which runs before every generate and verify. Whole-tree interaction with the existing rule, measured: planting `<prefix>_DB` into plan/inventory/identifiers.json made python3 plan/check.py --verify exit 1 with the single failure 'plan/inventory/identifiers.json:3559 names a legacy identifier (the predecessor system's identifier prefix); it is permitted only in docs/product-plan/reference/legacy-inventory.md, plan/gates.md, rust/crates/automonique-protocol/src/compat.rs, rust/crates/automonique-protocol/src/compat/generated.rs - use the neutral description here'; removing it returned exit 0. No file this item adds is in LEGACY_IDENTIFIER_HOMES and none needs to be. One repair this measurement caused: the drift message originally quoted the offending checked-in line verbatim, which would have put a planted identifier into a CI log. quotable() now scrubs the checked-in side before quoting it and prints '<redacted: ...>' instead; test_a_planted_identifier_is_not_echoed_by_the_drift_message asserts the value is absent from the message and test_an_ordinary_drift_message_still_quotes_the_line asserts an innocent difference is still quoted in full. One name is withheld rather than recorded: an unprefixed variable in the sanctioned inventory names a third-party product, which plan/gates.md#gate-scrub permits nowhere, so it is accounted for by SHA-256 fingerprint in a `withheld` row carrying no spelling. test_a_withheld_spelling_does_not_appear_in_the_output re-extracts the region, finds exactly one name whose digest is withheld, and asserts that name does not occur in the rendered document; grep for it in the file returns 0. test_a_withheld_fingerprint_matching_nothing_is_refused shows a withholding that protects no name fails the build as a dead permission.

Clean: python3 tools/identifiers/inventory.py verify exits 0 in 0.075 s with 'ok - plan/inventory/identifiers.json re-derives from 10 regions of docs/product-plan: 159 entries (140 durable, 17 compatibility-only, 2 presentation-only), 47 unclassified, 5 named gaps'. Deleting the file made verify exit 1 with 'plan/inventory/identifiers.json does not exist; run generate'; restoring returned exit 0. FORWARD, source loses a name: on a temporary copy of the corpus, replacing every '`legacyd`' with '`the daemon shim`' raised "region legacy-tokens declares 'legacyd' but no longer extracts it; a permitted source lost a name the inventory still classifies", and removing a cited evidence literal raised 'no longer has its evidence' (recorded under Source citation). Renaming the heading '## Normalized event model' raised "docs/product-plan/requirements/agent-integrations.md no longer contains the section '## Normalized event model'; the region that reads it would extract nothing", so a rotted parser fails loudly instead of quietly emitting less. Adding a crate line `automonique-brandnew/` changed the rendered bytes (a region with a default disposition absorbs it, and the checked-in copy then fails the forward check until it is regenerated and reviewed). consumers.R1-17: Read plan/inventory/identifiers.json. Two top-level views exist for this comparison. `durable_names` is a sorted array of every name classified durable (135 names). `compatibility_forwards` is an object mapping each of the 17 compatibility-only names to {"forwards_to": <durable name>, "also": [<durable name>, ...], "kind": <kind>}. The check 'no durable identifier is rewritten by this slice, proven by comparing the generated set against the R0-13 inventory' becomes: every CanonicalName::spelling() in rust/crates/automonique-protocol/src/compat/generated.rs must be a member of durable_names, and every LegacyName::spelling() must be a key of compatibility_forwards whose canonical().spelling() equals forwards_to or appears in also. That comparison was run here and passes on all four registry entries: AUTOMONIQUE_RUNNER, automonique doctor, automonique audit and automonique-shell are all in durable_names; LEGACY_RUNNER->AUTOMONIQUE_RUNNER, legacy:audit->automonique audit and legacy-shell->automonique-shell match forwards_to directly, and legacyctl matches through also (its primary forwards_to is `automonique`, because target-architecture.md installs it as a shim that execs `automonique <subcommand>`). tools/identifiers/test_inventory.py::ConsumerContract runs exactly this comparison against the checked-in registry today, so R1-17 can port it or call it. R1-17 must not treat this as its row being closed: this item did not touch rust/, and the row is R1-17's to measure in its own tree.
consumers.R1-19: `legacy_exceptions` is a sorted array of 17 rows, one per compatibility-only entry whose first segment is the compatibility namespace root, each carrying name, kind, forwards_to and authorized_by (the permitted source that binds it). That is the namespace gate's permitted exception set with its authorizing contract per row. R1-19 is already done and its inventory currently lives in rust/crates/automonique-protocol/src/namespace.rs; reconciling the two is R1-19's or the integrator's decision, not this item's, and this item claims nothing about R1-19's rows.

notes: What was built. plan/inventory/identifiers.json (4218 lines, 159246 bytes) is generated by tools/identifiers/inventory.py from ten named, deterministic parses of docs/product-plan/, checked in, and drift-checked in both directions. plan/inventory/README.md describes the shape and the two consumer contracts. tools/identifiers/test_inventory.py holds 42 tests, of which 18 are negative controls that break a rule, observe the named failure and restore. What is honestly open, stated first rather than buried. (1) 43 of the 57 environment-variable names are unclassified, not classified. docs/product-plan/reference/legacy-inventory.md lists the predecessor's product variables as suffixes of one uniform prefix and says R0-13 classifies each; docs/product-plan/requirements/operations-and-governance.md states the rule that would generate the pair (canonical AUTOMONIQUE_* resolved before legacy LEGACY_* fallback) but enumerates no suffix. Classifying them compatibility-only would create 43 dangling forwards, which the contract refuses; classifying them durable would assert 43 renames no document has made; deriving AUTOMONIQUE_<SUFFIX> and LEGACY_<SUFFIX> from the rule would be this item proposing 43 canonical variable names, which is invention, not derivation, and the contract says the inventory renames nothing. So each is recorded as an unclassified finding carrying the rule that will generate its pair once a work item declares it. That is the largest open number in this item and it is a real finding about the corpus, not a shortfall in the tool. The family pair itself (LEGACY_* -> AUTOMONIQUE_*) is fully sourced and is classified, so the environment-variable kind exercises the vocabulary. (2) Four further unclassified names: `legacy-run.sh` and `legacy.db` (path) and `legacy.*` and `legacy.runner.event` (protocol). Each is called a compatibility surface by a permitted source but has no canonical counterpart spelled anywhere in the corpus, so recording it compatibility-only would dangle. The protocol pair is the more interesting one: the corpus spells exactly one dotted canonical name, `automonique.dev-metrics/v1`, and none for the runtime wire protocols. (3) Five gaps are named in the file rather than implied: no legacy service name is inventoried, because legacy-inventory.md describes the predecessor's two units neutrally and spells neither; the 38 dashboard route paths are left out, because no source says whether each survives, forwards or is replaced; no canonical wire-protocol name exists beyond the metrics manifest; legacy-inventory.md heads its command list 'Commands (21)' and then lists 19, which is reported rather than reconciled because reconciling it would mean inventing two commands or editing a file outside this lease; and the backward direction of the drift check covers the ten regions, not the whole corpus - the legacy half is covered corpus-wide, the canonical half where the corpus enumerates it deterministically plus by forwarding closure. Scope choices a reviewer should look at first. (a) 76 names the corpus spells are recorded `out-of-scope` rather than classified: 57 version-1 table names absorbed by one declared family, 13 conversation route labels, and 6 namespace-root globs and SDK type aliases. A database table name, a conversation route label and a TypeScript type alias are none of the seven kinds the contract closes, and widening the kind set is not this item's to do. Every one is listed with its citation, and the family records everything it absorbed so absorption shows up in the diff. (b) `legacyctl` forwards to `automonique` rather than to `automonique doctor`, because target-architecture.md installs it as a thin shim that execs `automonique <subcommand>`; the six subcommand bindings other sources state are carried in forwards_to_also. R1-17's registry pairs it with `automonique doctor` alone, and that pairing is satisfied through `also`, so the comparison passes - but the two lists genuinely disagree about which is primary and this note is where that is recorded rather than smoothed over. (c) One name is withheld by fingerprint instead of recorded, because it names a third-party product and GATE-SCRUB permits those nowhere. That is a deliberate narrowing of the inventory and it is visible as a `withheld` row with its reason, not a silent omission. (d) The classification of the 19 legacy direct commands as durable rests on migration-plan.md 'Port the exact command registry before model-assisted routing' plus the pinned parity row; that is the weakest-sourced of the bulk classifications and is the first place a reviewer should push. What this item did not do: it renamed nothing, generated no compatibility codec, closed no gate, and touched no Rust, no Cargo manifest, no plan/check.py, no plan/work-graph.toml and no evidence file but its own. Wiring the drift check into plan/check.py is left for the integrator, as instructed.
